data.content_ref: inline:SRC_004's 'Cognitive Mirroring' argument proves too much in a way that defeats the requested evidence test. It frames confirmation bias as a structural property of autoregressive conditioning on prior tokens, but its own countercondition — a clean-slate checker context that erases the author's generation history — is exactly how a same-engine second pass is normally run, and the target gives no countable or executionable marker to decide whether a given same-engine check is still under 'gravity' or has escaped it. Without such a marker the claim that single-engine genuine verification is impossible is unfalsifiable in the record and provides no way, as the problem requires, to distinguish genuine independent verification from restatement within a single run; it also ignores that a separate engine can equally rubber-stamp, so separation is asserted as necessary without an in-record discriminator.
